It's an amazing game with superb potential and replay value. Only saying "it's a mix of GTA, Minecraft and Sim City" doesn't quite do it justice.
The strong suit being importing any lot you want from the workshop, build it, enter it, etc, all the while combating in the streets and making your legacy. Seamless transition between planning an attack, doing diplomacy, managing your territory.

Mostly meant as multiplayer with friends, but also very, very fun as a single player game!

As downsides, player/NPC models are reminiscent of early 2010s, and combat balance can feel like a hit or miss, and is quite punishing in early game.
It was enjoyable for a while.

I absolutely love this game, Also the insane amount of things made from scratch for this game is amazing. The developer is obviously very passionate about this project and the possible sequel.

Conceptually, it's a lot of things! It's not just "GTA meets Minecraft", the people who said that probably haven't tried Turf Zero, which is what I've spent about 17 hours on so far. Depending on who you are and how you play, it can be GTA, it can be Minecraft (with or without a city built up), it can be SimCity (mostly), it can be a large-scale strategy game, and it can be a (very) basic game about architecture.

What is it in practice? A mess of a game. Movement exists (and is floaty), guns go bang and need ammo, vehicles go vroom and drive and collide without causing the physics engine to panic, there's a well-thought-out wanted system that almost works consistently, you can earn and spend money, and there's a reputation system to encourage both taking out bandits and completing quests/missions. There are also some really high-level challenges (like military bases and dungeons) that are a massive difficulty spike from going up against bandits, but maybe they're doable with help.

What would I give this game? I'm not even sure. If you wanna see something cool that hasn't been done, but is far from "finished", go for it. I know I don't regret buying it.
